investigations.name: chemostat-equivalence
investigations.title: Chemostat equivalence: viva-biofilm vs analytic decay and real iDynoMiCS-2
investigations.objective:
Does the viva-biofilm Rust ChemostatProcess reproduce iDynoMiCS-2's
ChemostatSolver (first-order solute1 decay) to within 1% of the analytic
solution 2·e^(−0.1t)?

investigations.name: composability
investigations.title: Composability: a boundary controller process perturbing the biofilm at runtime
investigations.objective:
Does viva-biofilm's boundary_concentrations runtime hook (the Task 6
set_bulk_by_name binding) actually compose with an external
process-bigraph control process -- can a BoundaryControllerProcess drive
the biofilm's oxygen boundary on a schedule and produce a visible,
measurable growth response, the same way process-bigraph composes any two
processes sharing a store?

investigations.name: fig5-rs-ys-competition
investigations.title: RS vs YS competition: does seeding density decide the winner?
investigations.objective:
Cockx et al. 2024 (Fig. 5) report that when a Rate Strategist (RS — faster
growth, lower yield) competes against a Yield Strategist (YS — slower
growth, higher/more efficient yield) for a single shared oxygen substrate
in a 2D biofilm, the winner depends on seeding density: YS is favored at
low density, RS at intermediate density, YS favored again at high density.
Does viva-biofilm's multi-strategy competition engine — seeded with the
paper's exact Table-K RS/YS kinetics — reproduce a density-dependent
competition outcome, and in what direction?

investigations.name: runtime-and-scaling
investigations.title: Runtime and scaling: throughput and scaling curves for the Rust engine
investigations.objective:
After the ~23x performance pass and the addition of configurable PDE
parameters, how does the viva-biofilm engine's wall-time scale with grid
size, agent population, and run duration -- and what throughput
(agent-steps/sec) does it sustain?

investigations.name: spatial-biofilm-growth
investigations.title: Spatial biofilm growth: a developed colony with a real substrate gradient
investigations.objective:
Starting from a small inoculum of 40 agents, does the viva-biofilm spatial
engine grow a visibly developed 2D biofilm — hundreds of agents, a
measurable thickness above the substratum, and a genuine substrate-limitation
gradient (boundary richer than substratum) — within a short, deterministic,
non-swept run?
